note: Recast from the original description published by Scheffrahn (2010), in English, which gives prose descriptions and measurement tables for the soldier (two morphotypes) and for the worker; the alate is recorded there as Imago: unknown. The species is distinguished from all Neotropical Syntermitinae and Nasutitermitinae by the diameter of the nasus tip being greater than its mid-length diameter (the base is constricted). The measurements are copied in the mean±SD (range) form of the original.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldiers dimorphic, the two morphotypes morphologically almost identical and differing only in proportion; in the foraging groups collected, large and small soldiers were roughly equal in number. Head capsule orange or rusty orange, darker at the base of the nasus; the inflated apical part of the nasus is concolorous with the head capsule or paler, distinctly paler than its base. Head capsule hemispherical. Nasus extending far beyond the mandibles; the basal third slender, the diameter increasing after more than 1/3 of the length, greatest at about 2/3 of the length, then decreasing towards the tip to less than the basal diameter; the diameter at 2/3 is about 150% of the narrowest basal diameter. Nasus hollow, the outer wall of even thickness, circular in cross-section. Head capsule pilosity consisting of 2 longer hairs and usually 6 shorter hairs, arranged symmetrically left and right; the long hairs are on the vertex, above the plane of the nasus, the short hairs below that plane; the nasus is bare. Mandibles bent 160—190°, the greatest curvature behind the marginal tooth; mandibles becoming slender behind the marginal tooth; marginal tooth extremely long and narrow, the apical and marginal teeth extremely fine and pointed; when fully closed the mandibles do not overlap but continue to close and overlap near the marginal teeth. Antennae very long, almost 2 times the nasus length; 14 segments, 2<3>4<5=6. The process on the fore coxa is narrowly triangular, sharp and projecting forward. All legs long, the hind leg the longest. Anterior lobe of the pronotum abruptly upturned, dark and notched on both sides; posterior margin concave. Meso- and metanotum each with 2 lateral tubercles; the abdominal tergites also bear a row of smaller, weakly sclerotised lateral tubercles.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Worker monomorphic, slightly larger than the soldier. Head capsule rusty orange, but varying markedly in tone, from orange-yellow to chestnut brown. Head capsule with about 8 longer hairs and a few shorter hairs evenly distributed; two pairs of longer hairs visible in lateral view. Antenna 14 segments, 2<3>4=5. Fore coxa with a sharp swelling on the anterior margin. Enteric valve weakly sclerotised, the transition between P1 and P3 defined mainly by the constriction of the cuticular lining of P2; the enteric valve has 3 poorly defined pads, each with 12—16 very small triangular spines. Maximum worker head width (n=9, from 3 paratype colonies, mean±SD (range)) 1.11 mm±0.031 (1.06—1.15).

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Large soldier measurements (n=9, 3 from each paratype colony; mean±SD (range), mm): head length including nasus 2.02±0.084 (1.93—2.20); maximum head width 0.96±0.067 (0.89—1.09); maximum length of the left mandible 0.79±0.035 (0.74—0.84); nasus length 1.19±0.054 (1.11—1.26); narrowest basal diameter of the nasus 0.14±0.011 (0.12—0.15); widest apical diameter of the nasus 0.20±0.014 (0.17—0.22); maximum pronotum width 0.57±0.032 (0.52—0.62); fore tibia length 1.02±0.048 (0.96—1.11); hind tibia length 1.26±0.041 (1.21—1.36). Small soldier measurements (n=9, 3 from each paratype colony): head length including nasus 1.84±0.068 (1.74—1.93); maximum head width 0.84±0.070 (0.75—0.99); maximum length of the left mandible 0.72±0.058 (0.64—0.81); nasus length 1.11±0.030 (1.06—1.16); narrowest basal diameter of the nasus 0.12±0.0081 (0.10—0.12); widest apical diameter of the nasus 0.18±0.012 (0.16—0.20); maximum pronotum width 0.51±0.016 (0.48—0.53); fore tibia length 0.98±0.026 (0.93—1.01); hind tibia length 1.16±0.025 (1.14—1.21). Holotype large soldier: Buenavista, Sucre department, Colombia (9.31454, −75.02857), 2009-6-2, elevation 113 m, under cattle dung, collected by J. Chase (UF number CO-270). Alate unknown.
